::: {#exr-05-source-types-interactive}
## Source types, interactive

What is each kind of source good for? Drag it to its use. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "core",
   "label": "Core evidence"
  },
  {
   "id": "concepts",
   "label": "Concepts and methods"
  },
  {
   "id": "grey",
   "label": "Practice context — flag as grey"
  },
  {
   "id": "leads",
   "label": "Leads only — verify elsewhere"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "Peer-reviewed journals (IEEE TSE, Computers & Security)",
   "b": "core"
  },
  {
   "t": "Conference proceedings (ICSE, CHI, USENIX Security)",
   "b": "core"
  },
  {
   "t": "Books and textbooks",
   "b": "concepts"
  },
  {
   "t": "Standards and industry reports (NIST, OWASP, Verizon DBIR)",
   "b": "grey"
  },
  {
   "t": "Engineering blogs and vendor pages",
   "b": "leads"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Conference proceedings are core evidence in computing; grey literature gives practice context and must be flagged as such.",
 "ref": "sec-05-where-to-look",
 "reflabel": "Where to look"
}
</script>
</div>
```

::: {#exr-05-boolean-operators-interactive}
## Boolean operators, interactive

Sort each effect to the operator that produces it. Then press **Check**.

```{=html}
<div class="grc-ex" data-type="sort">
<script type="application/json">
{
 "buckets": [
  {
   "id": "and",
   "label": "AND"
  },
  {
   "id": "or",
   "label": "OR"
  },
  {
   "id": "not",
   "label": "NOT"
  }
 ],
 "chips": [
  {
   "t": "narrows the search",
   "b": "and"
  },
  {
   "t": "widens the search",
   "b": "or"
  },
  {
   "t": "excludes — use carefully",
   "b": "not"
  },
  {
   "t": "combines the concepts of the question",
   "b": "and"
  },
  {
   "t": "joins the synonyms within one concept",
   "b": "or"
  }
 ],
 "explain": "Synonyms within a concept are joined with OR; the concepts of the question are combined with AND.",
 "ref": "sec-05-systematic-search",
 "reflabel": "Systematic search"
}
</script>
</div>
```
:::
